raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## What does this PR do?

Changing `--seed` currently changes both model initialization and dataset shuffling/worker RNGs, so comparing weight initializations also changes the data stream.

Add optional `--data-seed` (`rng.data_seed` in config) to independently control dataset construction and DataLoader worker seeding. For example:

```bash
--seed 1234 --data-seed 5678
```

Holding `--data-seed` fixed allows changing the model/training seed while retaining the data stream. Omitting it preserves existing dataset seeds and worker seeding, including runtime parallel-rank offsets. The cyclic sampler’s existing epoch-based permutations are unchanged.

Wire the effective data seed through GPT, hybrid/Flex, BERT, T5, VLM, MiMO and finetuning data paths, offline cache preparation, and cached-logit dataset identity. Model initialization continues to use `--seed`. Document the CLI and cache/distillation behavior.

## Validation

- Passed 18 targeted tests in an isolated CPU harness. Actual Torch RNG/DataLoaders, NumPy, indexed/GPT/blended datasets, and compiled C++ dataset helpers executed; unavailable GPU runtime imports, distributed bootstrap, tokenizer setup, and unrelated CLI groups were isolated.
- Real indexed-data test: different model seeds with fixed data seed produce different weights but identical samples/cache hashes; a different data seed with fixed model seed changes samples/cache hashes while preserving weights.
- Cover CLI/config serialization, invalid seeds, worker RNG independence, legacy defaults, restored model RNG preservation during iterator creation, matching training/cache seeds, and cached-logit identity.
- `tools/autoformat.sh` passed Black, isort, pylint, Ruff, and mypy for changed unit tests. Ruff passed all changed production files. Python syntax and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full repository torchrun/GPU tests remain unrun locally:

```bash
python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node=8 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit_tests/data/test_data_samplers.py \
  tests/unit_tests/data/test_prepare_cache.py \
  tests/unit_tests/training/test_rng_ownership.py
```

 After initialization, data access is **read-only and lock-free**. Each data-parallel rank consumes a disjoint subset of samples, and no cross-rank coordination is needed during training because all ranks derive the same deterministic permutation from a shared random seed.
 
+## Separate Model and Data Seeds
+
+`--seed` controls model initialization and the training RNGs. Set `--data-seed` to a
+positive integer to independently seed dataset construction (including shuffle indices,
+masking, and FIM) and DataLoader workers:
+
+```bash
+torchrun ... pretrain_gpt.py --seed 1234 --data-seed 5678 ...

+Hold `--data-seed` fixed while varying `--seed` to compare weight initializations on the

+`--seed`, and DataLoader workers use the model-seeded PyTorch RNG's initial seed.
+The cyclic batch sampler's existing epoch-based permutations are unchanged.
+
+Use the same `--data-seed` when preparing caches with `tools/prepare_cache.py` and when
+resuming training. Custom external dataloaders own their seeding; they can use
+`get_run_config().rng.effective_data_seed` to honor this option.
